chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him), saying: 'If I am on the road to Mecca and we descend for prayer in places where there are Bedouins, should we pray the obligatory prayer on the ground, reciting the Mother of the Book alone, or should we pray upon the ride, reciting the Opening of the Book and the Chapter?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you fear, pray the obligatory and non-obligatory prayers upon the ride; and when you recite Al-Hamd and a Chapter, it is more beloved to me, and I do not see any problem with what you do.'

key_terms.أُمَّ الْكِتَاب: The Mother of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying on a mount versus on the ground during travel in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the flexibility in prayer postures during travel, distinguishing between the obligatory concession for fear (Salat al-Khauf) and the general permissibility of praying on one's mount. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms that while praying on the mount is preferred in states of fear, performing full prayer on the ground with complete recitation is equally valid and beloved, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease and the absence of rigid restriction in travel prayers.
